title: Lift and reconstruction experiments with explicit hypothesis boundaries

concepts.label: audited expansion claim boundary
concepts.note: A distinction between an exact Lean declaration, supporting proof substrate, finite checked instances, measurements, and any claim that would resolve an open Erdős problem.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED: allRight_landingExcess_two_impossible derives False only from its displayed all-right, landing-excess-two, and three-row cofactor-support hypotheses. It does not state that a survivor set is empty.
open_antecedents: hright: the seam word extends right at every row from D+1 onward
hcof: the required cofactor ranks lie in the seam-word support on rows D+1 through D+3
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: No priority or novelty claim is made. This node records the exact scope needed for public claim hygiene.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The audit found the cofactor-support hypothesis false at D = 101, 122, 164, 314, 545, 629, and 1112, and found no observed landing seam excess equal to two in s = 5..102. Those observations are audit evidence, not additional Lean theorems.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED: for a pulse sequence bounded above by Q, a ratchet orbit starting at b₀ at least Q+2 cannot return to its initial value at a positive time.
open_antecedents: hQ: P s ≤ Q for every row s
statement_nodes.engine: monotone lower bound for the imported Recon257 ratchet
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: No priority or novelty claim is made. This node records the exact scope needed for public claim hygiene.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The theorem applies only in the large-offset region b₀ ≥ Q+2. It does not cover the live offsets 1 through 9. The separate universal-barrier theorem has an unsatisfied initial hypothesis for the concrete use discussed in the audit.
